add.text:
Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""
S1. Yeah, so the difference between the V1 and V2 is tremendous.
S2. The V1 is much more compact.
S3. And it's not doing the refinement.
S4. So, Yeah, these cards on the V2 page, I see a list here, one, number one, number two, number three.
S5. It's not using an actual list.
S6. I don't know if we're rendering these as markdown.
S7. I don't know how these are being created, like the V2 cards.
S8. Again, these should be prompt instances, and the underlying data structure for both of those systems needs to be unified.
S9. I think I've already said that we need that to be clear.
S10. When we're creating prompts, when we're kind of restructuring the prompts into a new prompt, we could break out a new sentence into a new prompt card, or it just gets added to the old one until it becomes clear.
S11. I think the live agent should do the best it can kind of per sentence and not try to do anything after that.
S12. So that then it's doing more of the real-time, quick pass.
S13. So each sentence gets placed properly.
S14. And then I think we wanna leave it to the smart mastermind to create the proper titles and to kind of do a more thorough and proper restructuring of the prompt.
S15. And doing that properly, meaning the fast assistant does what it should be doing and the smart assistant does what it should be doing and it does it reliably, I think is important.
S16. Now, I don't know how we merge these.
S17. Well, okay, so for these refined prompts, these, like, summary, paragraph, title and paragraph
S18. It says show raw underneath each one.
S19. I mean, it's kind of what I was asking for, but it's not really, well, number one, it's not browsable.
S20. I mean, text and then underneath that see each sentence kind of broken down.
S21. And I think there might have been some...
S22. No, I guess that's it.
S23. So it's just...
S24. Yeah, the raw transcription for... each one of those cards is not very helpful.
S25. I mean, I'd hope that we're adequately kind of capturing all of the necessary tasks and whatnot, but we need to focus on that system too.
S26. Prompt refinement in terms of titles and paragraphs, summaries that have this show raw button underneath, are these actual prompt instances from the session log?
S27. And if not, they should be.
S28. And then the way that the chat bubbles are being rendered, and those are being rendered, we kind of want to unify that experience, like that we can still have a V1 and V2 in terms of a slightly different UI
S29. However, the internal... well, okay, for one, the V2 page does not show the live raw transcription from Whisper like the V1 does.
S30. And that's very helpful 'cause I can see that it's working.
S31. I can see that, okay, it's actually transcribed and what I'm saying, somebody's hearing me.
S32. And that's very important.
S33. When I go over the V2 page, I scroll to the bottom and I see an idle task, and yeah, in terms of spawning, the task is spawn fresh child agents, stop reviving old sessions.
S34. It's not a law that we can't ever revive an old session, but generally, for accounting, it should be noted that when you revive, if you revive an old session, especially, yeah, when you revive an old session that you haven't created, then it's cost and completion accounting is then misattributed.
S35. Anything new that happens in there gets attributed to the past, whoever spawned it.
S36. Now for quick questions, if you're trying to figure out how something was done or whatever, I don't necessarily mind it.
S37. If it's just quicker and easier.
S38. However, it shouldn't be for building new things is basically the idea.
S39. We want new, and you definitely, well, probably should not give it a task.
S40. If it's a quick fix task, fine, whatever.
S41. It's misaccounted, whatever.
S42. But then that task gets misattributed.
S43. And so, whether the task is complete or not, it's, if somebody is looking for that task in the session that asked for it, it's just not going to exist because the task would have to get handed to the other one.
S44. Anyway, yeah, but in terms of the experience here on the V2 page, we definitely need to see the live transcriptions appearing on screen.
S45. And then my gut tells me that the way that the live transcriptions, a lot of sentences, it's like a flood of sentences, they need to start getting kind of merged into these refined title and paragraphs in a way where they kind of disappear inside it.
S46. And frankly, that's how it's set up right now.
S47. We have this... we have the show raw that is the expanded view.
S48. And inside of that, we have the actual raw transcripts.
S49. So in a way, that's kind of how it works is the raw transcripts get tucked into these little summary cards.
S50. Now the problem is, yeah, I mean, the summaries that you're giving aren't bad.
S51. There's a lot of words underneath.
S52. I kind of just want to see kind of the conclusive outcomes as simply as possible, kind of in a ranked way.
S53. And so it seems like we're not really trying to refine these outcomes.
S54. Refined prompt cards.
S55. We just keep adding to the list.
S56. We want to converge.
S57. We want to reduce the amount of content.
S58. We don't want to always be just creating new shit.
S59. We want to be producing useful outcomes, and I need to see kind of what decisions are on the table as I'm dictating in real time like this.
S60. The V2 page should be giving me as much current accurate information as possible, answering questions, etc.
S61. If I ask a question, I want to see it appear on the screen as quickly as possible.
S62. I think part of that is that the timeout to send after pause might be too high.
S63. But I'm also thinking that maybe the...
S64. Well, okay, so if the fast assistant is able to identify a question properly, which it should be, it should be able to take the structured sentences.
S65. And if one of the sentences is actually a question, it can turn it into a question instance.
S66. And then that question instance could be... well, the smart assistant should see those being created in real time.
S67. Well, okay.
S68. So...
S69. I actually don't know how I feel about that.
S70. Answer me, does the smart assistant tail the fast assistant's work?
S71. So, as the fast assistant is creating prompt instances, and well, amending them, essentially adding the sentence stream, it adds it to the last prompt or maybe creates a new prompt.
S72. But these prompt instances, is the smart assistant tailing its own session.jsonl?
S73. Because that was one of the ways in which it could receive updates.
S74. I actually don't mind it.
S75. That actually might not be bad.
S76. I actually don't mind it.
S77. I think it's a little bit more token heavy, but I think that's actually maybe not the worst way to do it.
S78. So...
S79. After the fast assistant refines each sentence, basically, it automatically gets pushed into the smart assistant who can then answer the question.
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
